text: Sometimes you don't want one output row per value -- you want every value in a group collapsed into a single, readable string. STRING_AGG does exactly that: every color a product subcategory comes in, joined into one comma-separated line per subcategory.

STRING_AGG is itself an aggregate function. It sits in the SELECT list right alongside GROUP BY, same as SUM or COUNT -- it just returns a joined string instead of a number, using whatever separator you pass as the second argument.

On its own, the order those values get joined in isn't guaranteed. Add WITHIN GROUP with an ORDER BY, and now the concatenation order is explicit and repeatable -- here, alphabetically by color, every time you run it.

And one convenience worth knowing: STRING_AGG skips NULL values automatically, exactly like other aggregates do. You don't need a WHERE clause filtering them out first -- they're simply left out of the joined string, with no stray separator left behind.
Next up, the reverse operation: STRING_SPLIT, which takes one string and breaks it back apart into rows.
